Fri

Sep 4OUTBOUND DAYMedium-low confidenceSep 4 · 06:00–22:00 ET
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KLZU observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. KLZU has no TAF station, so KPDK is used as a proxy. It is the strongest flight-category evidence this page can show. Beyond the TAF horizon of about 30 hours; no TAF exists at this range for any station.
NWS-hr
NWS hourly gridpoint forecast — the National Weather Service digital forecast for the grid cell containing KLZU, updated through the day and reaching about 156 hours. It gives hour-by-hour sky, wind and precipitation probability, and it is the spine of the change windows on this board. The NWS hourly gridpoint forecast reaches this day.
NWS-day
NWS day/night outlook — the same National Weather Service grid summarised into day and night halves, reaching about 168 hours. Coarser than the hourly product but it covers one day further, so this page uses it only to describe spans the hourly forecast cannot reach. Not needed: this day is already covered by the finer-resolution hourly gridpoint forecast.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued by the National Weather Service four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this page uses it to corroborate the flight category. Beyond the GFS MAV MOS horizon of about 72 hours, or no MAV row carried both a ceiling and a visibility for this day.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This page shows it only as a flagged outlook and never promotes it into a short-range category. An extended GFS MEX outlook point describes part of this day. MEX publishes no ceiling or visibility, so it states no flight category; where its sky, precipitation, thunderstorm or obstruction fields are usable it is shown as a clearly labelled “(Predicted)” value.
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KLZU this run.

METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KLZU observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. KLZU has no TAF station, so KPDK is used as a proxy. It is the strongest flight-category evidence this page can show. Beyond the TAF horizon of about 30 hours; no TAF exists at this range for any station.
NWS-hr
NWS hourly gridpoint forecast — the National Weather Service digital forecast for the grid cell containing KLZU, updated through the day and reaching about 156 hours. It gives hour-by-hour sky, wind and precipitation probability, and it is the spine of the change windows on this board. The NWS hourly gridpoint forecast reaches this day.
NWS-day
NWS day/night outlook — the same National Weather Service grid summarised into day and night halves, reaching about 168 hours. Coarser than the hourly product but it covers one day further, so this page uses it only to describe spans the hourly forecast cannot reach. The coarse NWS day/night outlook describes part of this day.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued by the National Weather Service four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this page uses it to corroborate the flight category. Beyond the GFS MAV MOS horizon of about 72 hours, or no MAV row carried both a ceiling and a visibility for this day.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This page shows it only as a flagged outlook and never promotes it into a short-range category. An extended GFS MEX outlook point describes part of this day. MEX publishes no ceiling or visibility, so it states no flight category; where its sky, precipitation, thunderstorm or obstruction fields are usable it is shown as a clearly labelled “(Predicted)” value.
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. This period is past the 144-hour end of the published WPC surface prog series, so no chart covers it. That is the product's horizon, not a failure, and it says nothing about the weather.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KLZU this run.

Extended outlook summary

.. (This afternoon through Tuesday) Issued at 230 PM EDT Mon Aug 31 2026 The expansive upper ridge over the south-central U.S. — .. (Wednesday morning through next Sunday) Issued at 230 PM EDT Mon Aug 31 2026 Dry and Warm Weather Through Mid-Week: The expansive mid-level ridge will slide east on Wednesday, centering over the central and southern Appalachians.

Short term

.. (This afternoon through Tuesday) Issued at 230 PM EDT Mon Aug 31 2026 The expansive upper ridge over the south-central U.S. will continue to build eastward through Tuesday. Temperatures will notch higher on Tuesday as a result, bringing high temperatures into the mid 90s for most areas outside of the mountains. Heat index values will also push near or over 100 degrees for most of these areas as well by Tuesday afternoon, though short of Heat Advisory criteria of 105. As far as any potential for rainfall is concerned, it'll be few and far between. While a rogue shower or brief thunderstorm can't be entirely ruled out through this evening, mainly in the northeast Georgia mountains or far southeast counties, Tuesday will bring even less potential with the vast majority of locations remaining dry as subsidence increases further.

Long term

.. (Wednesday morning through next Sunday) Issued at 230 PM EDT Mon Aug 31 2026 Dry and Warm Weather Through Mid-Week: The expansive mid-level ridge will slide east on Wednesday, centering over the central and southern Appalachians. For North and Central GA, this will result in another warm and mostly rain-free day. Tropical moisture from over the Atlantic/Florida will start to push northward into the southern side of the ridge, so we can't rule out some afternoon showers and storms in far southeast areas. High temps will remain in the low to mid 90s, with heat index values peaking around 100-105. Rain/Thunderstorm Potential Returns Late Week into the Weekend: Uncertainty in the forecast jumps up substantially for the Thu/Fri time period, as models have significant spread in how the synoptic pattern evolves. Over the past 24 hours, there has been an uptick in the number of ensemble members that have a shortwave trough and slug of tropical moisture surging up across Florida into Georgia and squeezing out the mid-level ridge. With PWAT values of 2-2.5", this would support numerous to widespread showers and storms each day, becoming isolated to scattered over the weekend as moisture decreases. On the flip side, there is still a group of ensemble members that have the ridge holding in place and shunting the tropical moisture off to the southwest, which would keep rain chances very low over our area. With either solution (and anything in between), temperatures will remain at or above normal through the weekend, with highs in the upper 80s to low 90s. Confidence in the late week / weekend forecast will continue to grow over the next 24- 48 hours, so stay tuned for updates!

METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KAVL observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Sep 2 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Sep 1 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: RATE_LIMITED), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KROA observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Sep 2 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Sep 1 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: RATE_LIMITED), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KGKT observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Sep 2 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category. This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KTYS is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Sep 1 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KGKT this run.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KSHD observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Sep 2 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category. This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KCHO is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Sep 1 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KSHD this run.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KSSI observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Sep 2 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Sep 1 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: RATE_LIMITED), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KJZI observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Sep 2 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Sep 1 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KJZI this run.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KHXD observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Sep 2 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category. This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KSAV is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Sep 1 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KHXD this run.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KFIN observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Sep 2 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category. This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KDAB is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Sep 1 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KFIN this run.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KMYR observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Sep 2 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Sep 1 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KMYR this run.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KCRE observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Sep 2 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category. This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KMYR is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Sep 1 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KCRE this run.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KCRG observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Sep 2 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Sep 1 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KCRG this run.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KPNS observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Sep 2 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Sep 1 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KPNS this run.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KSPG observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Sep 2 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category. This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KPIE is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Sep 1 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. The NOTAM query failed this run (state: RATE_LIMITED), so the NOTAM list is unknown rather than empty.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KTPF observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Sep 2 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category. This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KTPA is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Sep 1 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KTPF this run.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KVNC observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Sep 2 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category. This airport has no TAF station of its own, so KSRQ is used as a proxy; that is a normal condition, not a failure.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Sep 1 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KVNC this run.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KJKA observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Sep 2 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Sep 1 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KJKA this run.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KBFM observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Sep 2 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Sep 1 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KBFM this run.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KNEW observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Sep 2 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Sep 1 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KNEW this run.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KOPF observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Sep 2 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Sep 1 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KOPF this run.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KHPN observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Sep 2 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Sep 1 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KHPN this run.

Forecast evidence
METAR
METAR — the routine surface observation issued hourly by the reporting station, with SPECI reports off-cycle, carrying ceiling, visibility, wind, temperature and altimeter. Issued by the observing station and distributed by aviationweather.gov. This is measured fact, not a forecast, and on this page it describes conditions right now, not this day. A current KBED observation was read this run. It describes conditions now, not this trip day.
TAF
TAF — the Terminal Aerodrome Forecast, the highest-resolution aviation forecast available. The National Weather Service issues it four times a day, valid 24 to 30 hours, with explicit FM and TEMPO change groups. Airports without their own TAF station use a nearby proxy, which is a normal condition and not a fault. Beyond the 30 h TAF horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Wed Sep 2 · 6:00 PM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.
MAV
GFS MOS (MAV) — Model Output Statistics, the GFS model bias-corrected against decades of observations at this station. Issued four times a day in three-hourly steps out to about 72 hours. It carries an explicit ceiling and visibility category, so this card uses it to resolve a day the TAF cannot reach. Beyond the 72 h GFS MOS horizon at this lead time. The product published normally; this day is simply past its reach, which is expected and is not a fault. Expected to be covered from about Tue Sep 1 · 12:00 AM ET. The extended GFS MOS (MEX) outlook does reach this day and is shown as a labelled rough outlook; it never states a flight category.
MEX
GFS extended MOS (MEX) — the extended-range MOS product, issued twice a day in twelve-hourly steps out to about 192 hours. Coarse, but the only station-calibrated numeric guidance that reaches the far end of a long weekend. This card shows it only as a labelled rough outlook and never as a resolved forecast. A station-calibrated MEX MOS product was read for this airport this run (state: ok).
GFA
GFA and prog charts — the Graphical Forecast for Aviation and the Weather Prediction Center surface progs, issued by the National Weather Service through the day; the surface prog series reaches 144 hours. They are raster images a pilot reads for fronts, pressure systems and precipitation shields. This page displays them with their issuing office and valid time and never interprets them: no category, wind, ceiling, ranking or go/no-go here is derived from an image. A published WPC surface chart matches this period and is shown in the dropdown with its issuing office and valid time. It is displayed, never interpreted.
NOTAM
FAA NOTAM (NMS) — Notices to Air Missions: closures, outages, obstacles and TFRs, issued continuously by the FAA and valid until cancelled. On this page they are advisory evidence about the airport, not weather, and they never change a flight category. NOTAMs were read for KBED this run.

4 · Planning gates

  • Evidence gate: an unavailable, stale, or out-of-horizon source is unknown — never treat it as favorable.
  • Weather gate: compare current observations and valid-period forecasts with personal ceiling, visibility, convection, wind, and crosswind minimums.
  • Route gate: screen the actual route, altitude, and time against official hazard products; feed totals on this page are not route-filtered.
  • Operations gate: verify NOTAMs, TFRs, runway conditions, fuel, aircraft performance, daylight, and alternates.

5 · ForeFlight manual cross-check (before flight)

  • Official briefing matches these go/no-go windows
  • Prog charts / radar / satellite trend agrees with convection timing
  • Winds & temps aloft along actual route (may shift ETE)
  • NOTAMs & TFRs — airport-scoped NMS records may be shown, but route-wide/TFR coverage is not included; pull a fresh official briefing for departure, destination, and alternates
  • Runway condition / length / closures at destination & alternate
  • Weight & balance + performance at forecast density altitude (heat!)
  • File & brief in ForeFlight; confirm fuel stops if long-range

Everything the page does

  • Mission Control with destination and day selection, fail-closed category ranges, a keyboard- and touch-operable schematic airport map, filters, clustering, and a synchronized text list
  • Per-source state, validity horizon, and target-date coverage for every destination
  • Explicit unavailable/out-of-horizon target cells; no static weather fallback
  • Per-airport expandable detail — current observations, covered forecasts, dep/dest METAR temperatures
  • Current-and-future KLZU board with four fixed 06:00–22:00 ET boxes and outbound/return day context
  • Source-labelled TAF/MOS flight-category guidance only when a source interval actually covers the visible standard box — a box with no covering interval shows an explicit unavailable/out-of-horizon state instead of a category, never an implied one
  • Timed NWS weather, wind-favored runway (magnetic, from each airport's own runways), gust, and material crosswind context wherever the forecast supplies them
  • Raw METAR/TAF + data-sources dropdown per airport
  • FAA Airport Status & Delays with known, unsupported, and unavailable states
  • Best-effort 100LL fuel prices
  • Auto-refreshed about 4x a day by an hourly scheduler that republishes once 6 h have passed since the last publish, so refresh times drift; the last-updated stamp is exact and the next-run stamp is an estimate
  • Quick links (Flight Circle, ForeFlight, FlightAware) + Feedback
  • FAA chart-cycle stamp (current VFR Sectional + Chart Supplement)
  • Published PDF download plus browser print fallback — print-ready, color-preserving (semantic colors kept on paper)
  • Deterministic evidence-backed page; external AI aviation prose is withheld pending a validated evidence schema, so the executive-summary region shows an explicit pending-feature placeholder instead of generated text
  • Model-labeled MOS target-window outlook per airport (Iowa State GFS with conditional GFS Extended/MEX), with runtime and validity horizon shown
  • Expandable NWS FFC pattern summary and extended outlook inside the KLZU board
  • Per-airport chart links: SkyVector & AirNav/Chart Supplement (deep links)
  • FAA NMS owner-approved production source NOTAM adapter with explicit per-airport source states; active on this page as the owner-approved production source, and never a substitute for an official briefing
  • Full run archive: run_manifest.json with all data + provenance log
